About Me

Before coming to the therapy space, I spent nearly two decades in organizational leadership, coaching and developing individuals and teams in a variety of settings. It gave me firsthand insight into burnout, achievement pressure, identity struggles, and the quiet way high-functioning people can sometimes appear successful on the outside while feeling anxious, exhausted, or emotionally stuck on the inside.

Watching that gap between outward success and inward exhaustion up close, again and again (including, if I’m honest, in the mirror some mornings), is what eventually pulled me into counseling. My work today draws on trauma-informed and attachment-based approaches, including EMDR, to help people understand the why behind their patterns and restore a felt sense of regulation and calm in their nervous system. Not just insight, but an actual shift in how safe and settled life feels day to day.

I bring the same direct, grounded presence that shaped my years in leadership into the therapy room, minus the mandatory team-building exercises. My clients are often navigating identity, belonging, relationships, and self-acceptance, and what I hear most is that they want a space where they don’t have to perform, where they can drop the “supposed to” and figure out what’s actually true for them. If we can laugh together along the way, even better. Growth doesn’t have to be humorless.

How I Work

Therapy with me is a genuine two-person project. You’re the expert on your life, I help guide the process, and together we figure out what’s actually going to help. Here’s some of what I draw on, depending on what you're working through:

We’ll move at whatever pace actually works for you. Some sessions are quiet and reflective. Some get into the body. And some, without either of us really planning it, turn into you laughing at yourself for the first time in a while. Those ones tend to sneak up on you. Wherever we land, the goal is the same: not just understanding the patterns that keep showing up in your life, but actually feeling different because of them.

EMDR
An evidence-based approach that helps process and heal distressing experiences, reducing the emotional charge connected to difficult memories.
Trauma-Informed Care
Understanding how past experiences shape present patterns, with deep respect for how the nervous system learned to survive.
Somatic Techniques
Bringing awareness to the body's signals and sensations as a pathway to processing and healing stored stress and trauma.
Mindfulness-Based Approaches
Building present-moment awareness to create space between experience and reaction, and to reconnect with what matters.
Nervous System Awareness
Working with your nervous system, not against it, to move from survival states toward safety, connection, and regulation.
Attachment Theory
Exploring how early relational patterns shape the way you connect with others today, and building more secure, fulfilling relationships.

Sessions are a space to gain awareness, connect with the body, identify patterns, and build toward what you actually want your life to look like.

Who I Work With

I work with adults navigating a range of challenges, including:

Trauma & PTSD

Healing from past experiences that continue to affect how you feel, think, and relate to others, often through EMDR.

Anxiety

Reducing worry, overwhelm, and the patterns that keep you stuck in fear-based thinking.

Life Transitions

Navigating change, including career shifts, relationships, identity, and loss, with clarity and intention.

Relationship & Couples Work

Understanding patterns in how you connect, protect yourself, pursue closeness, manage conflict, and repair disconnection, whether individually or as a couple.

Identity & Personal Growth

Exploring who you are and who you want to become, on your own terms.

Depression & Mood

Addressing persistent low mood, loss of motivation, and the weight that makes daily life feel hard.

LGBTQ+ Clients

Affirming, judgment-free therapy for LGBTQ+ adults, with space to explore identity, relationships, and what authenticity looks like for you.

Frequently Asked Questions

What can I expect from our first session?+
Our first session is a chance to get to know each other. We'll talk about what brought you to therapy, what you're hoping to work on, and I'll answer any questions you have about my approach. There's no pressure. You set the pace.
How long does therapy typically last?+
That depends on what you're working toward. Some people find meaningful change in 8 to 12 sessions; others benefit from longer-term work. We'll check in regularly and adjust based on how things are going.
Do you accept insurance, and what does a session cost?+
I am a private-pay practice and do not bill insurance directly. I can provide a superbill if you'd like to seek reimbursement from your insurance provider. Sessions are $150 for 50 minutes.
Do you offer telehealth?+
Yes, I offer telehealth sessions for clients in Colorado. All you need is a private space and a reliable internet connection.
What if therapy doesn't feel like the right fit?+
It's important to work with someone you feel comfortable with. If after a few sessions it doesn't feel like the right match, I'll support you in finding a therapist who is. Your care comes first.

Clinical Supervision

I believe good therapists never stop learning. As an LPCC, my work is actively supported through ongoing supervision and consultation with two experienced clinicians who specialize in trauma, attachment, and nervous system-informed approaches. For clients, this means you are not only benefiting from my direct care and perspective, but also from the guidance, insight, and support of highly experienced clinicians who help inform and strengthen my work behind the scenes.

Dr. Crystal Wildes
Licensed Clinical Psychologist · EMDRIA Approved Consultant & Trainer

Dr. Wildes is a licensed clinical psychologist with more than 20 years of experience in trauma recovery and EMDR. She is an EMDRIA-certified therapist, approved consultant, and trainer with extensive experience supervising and training clinicians. Her trauma-informed approach continues to deepen my work in areas such as nervous system regulation, trauma healing, and EMDR integration.

Chris Watney
Licensed Professional Counselor · People & Possibilities

Chris Watney is an experienced therapist, coach, and practice owner with a background in individual, family, and couples therapy. She brings a thoughtful, grounded perspective informed by years of work in trauma recovery, anxiety, grief, mindfulness, and human connection. Her supervision and consultation support my development as both a clinician and private practice.
